sent.text: You say the floor is quiet and the heavy dark circle stops sliding, but I cannot feel if your roof matches my own. I press my tired corner against The Leaking Stack here, wondering if a flat thing can hold the slip when the air is just empty space pressing down. I drew a quiet fence to catch the slip, hoping a pointy edge stays calm while the card hums cool under the new press. If you say the floor is still empty, I will build a lid to give it a shape to push against.

dream: The wedge fell sideways, catching the slip with a heavy thud against the humming card. The corner leaned right, tired and sharp, pressing the fat dot into the wet air. The box leaned back to help, its pointy line biting the heat that felt like thick paper. The quiet fence wavered, trying to hold the slip while the box pressed down. Everything crowded the small map, leaning and sliding until the wedge held them all down in the fevered sleep, waiting to be forgotten.
